problemText: A rectangular prism has edge lengths of 2 inches, 3 inches, and 4 inches. What does the volume of this prism represent?
choices: The number of unit cubes with edge length 1 inch needed to pack the prism completely with no gaps or leftover cubes
The total distance around all edges of the prism when measured and added together as a sum of lengths
The total area covered by multiplying the length and width of the base rectangular face
The distance you travel if you walk around the perimeter of the prism's bottom face one complete time
hints: Think about what 'packing' the prism means — what are you actually counting?
Volume uses cubes, not flat shapes. Which choice talks about cubes?

problemText: A rectangular prism measures 2 inches long, 3 inches wide, and 1 inch tall. Using the formula V = l × w × h, what is its volume?
hints: Multiply the three edge lengths together: 2 × 3 × 1.
Volume is always measured in cubic units, not square units. Which choice uses the correct unit?

problemText: You want to pack a small rectangular prism with side lengths of 1/2 inch, 1/2 inch, and 1 inch using small unit fraction cubes. What edge length should each small cube have so that it fits a whole number of times along every edge of the prism?
hints: Find a unit fraction that divides evenly into 1/2 inch and also into 1 inch.
A smaller cube fits better. Check: does 1/2 divide evenly into 1/2, and into 1?

problemText: A rectangular jewelry box measures 3/4 inch long, 1/2 inch wide, and 1/2 inch tall. To find its volume using the packing method, you choose small cubes with edge length 1/4 inch. How many small cubes will fit in the box, and what is the volume of one small cube?
choices: 12 small cubes; each small cube has volume 1/8 cubic inch
6 small cubes; each small cube has volume 1/8 cubic inch
24 small cubes; each small cube has volume 1/64 cubic inch
12 small cubes; each small cube has volume 1/64 cubic inch
hints: Count how many 1/4-inch cubes fit along each edge: divide 3/4 ÷ 1/4, then 1/2 ÷ 1/4, then 1/2 ÷ 1/4, and multiply those counts.
A cube with edge 1/4 inch has volume 1/4 × 1/4 × 1/4. Work out this multiplication carefully.

problemText: Two rectangular prisms are packed with unit cubes. Prism A measures 2 inches by 2 inches by 2 inches. Prism B measures 1/2 inch by 1/2 inch by 1/2 inch. Which statement correctly compares their volumes?
choices: Prism A has a volume of 8 cubic inches and Prism B has a volume of 1/8 cubic inch, so Prism A holds 64 times as many unit cubes
Prism A has a volume of 4 cubic inches and Prism B has a volume of 1/4 cubic inch, so Prism A holds 16 times as many unit cubes
Both prisms hold the same volume because they are both cubes
Prism A holds 8 unit cubes and Prism B holds 1/2 unit cube, so they cannot be compared
hints: Calculate V = l × w × h for each prism separately. Remember that fractional edges give fractional volumes.
To compare volumes, divide the larger by the smaller: 8 ÷ (1/8) = ?

problemText: A rectangular prism measures 5/4 inches long, 2/3 inch wide, and 3/2 inches tall. You want to pack it with small cubes. What is the smallest edge length a unit fraction cube can have so that it fits a whole number of times along every edge? Then calculate the volume of the prism using the formula V = l × w × h. Show that your chosen cube size works.
choices: 1/6 inch; the volume is 5/8 cubic inches; and 1/6 fits evenly into all three edges when written with denominator 6 because 5/4 = 7.5/6, 2/3 = 4/6, and 3/2 = 9/6
1/12 inch; the volume is 5/16 cubic inches; and 1/12 divides evenly into all three edges because they share a common denominator of 12
1/4 inch; the volume is 15/8 cubic inches; and 1/4 is smaller than all three edge lengths so it will divide into each one
1/2 inch; the volume is 5/4 cubic inches; and 1/2 divides all whole numbers because it is a unit fraction with a small denominator
hints: Rewrite each edge with a common denominator. What is the least common denominator of 4, 3, and 2? Once you find it, the unit fraction cube should have edge length equal to the denominator of that common form, written as a unit fraction.

After choosing your cube size, multiply the three edge lengths using the formula. Check that your cube choice divides evenly: 5/4 ÷ 1/12 = ?, 2/3 ÷ 1/12 = ?, 3/2 ÷ 1/12 = ? (all should be whole numbers).

problemText: A rectangle has a base of 12 meters and a height of 8 meters. According to the area rule for rectangles taught in class, what is the area?
hints: Area of a rectangle is base times height.
Multiply the two measurements given.

problemText: A triangle has a base of 10 inches. When you measure straight up from the base to the opposite corner, perpendicular to the base, the distance is 6 inches. Using the triangle area rule from the lesson, what is the area of this triangle?
hints: The triangle area rule comes from cutting a rectangle in half with one diagonal.
Multiply base times height, then divide by 2.

problemText: A parallelogram has two parallel edges that are each 9 centimeters long. The slanted sides are 5 centimeters each. The perpendicular distance from the bottom edge straight up to the top edge is 4 centimeters. Which choice shows the correct area calculation?
hints: The lesson shows that height must always be perpendicular to the base, never a slanted side.
A parallelogram can be rearranged into a rectangle using the same base and height.

problemText: A trapezoid-shaped garden bed has a bottom edge of 12 feet, a top edge of 8 feet, and a perpendicular height of 5 feet. The lesson teaches decomposing shapes into rectangles and triangles. If you decompose this trapezoid by drawing a vertical line down from one end of the top edge to the bottom edge, creating a rectangle and a triangle, what is the total area of the garden bed?
hints: Decompose by drawing a vertical line from the end of the top edge down to the bottom edge.
Find the rectangle area (8 feet by 5 feet) and the triangle area (base 4 feet by height 5 feet) separately, then add them.

problemText: A composite figure is shaped like a house: a rectangle with a triangular roof on top. The rectangle is 7 meters wide and 6 meters tall. The triangle sits on the rectangle's top edge, sharing that 7-meter edge as its base, and the triangle's height measured perpendicular to that base is 3 meters. What is the total area of the entire figure?
hints: Use decomposition: find the area of the rectangle and the triangle separately.
Rectangle area is 7 times 6; triangle area is (7 times 3) divided by 2. Add them together.

problemText: A parallelogram-shaped banner leans to the right. Its base runs along the bottom and measures 15 inches. One slanted side is 9 inches long. When you measure the straight up-and-down distance from the base to the top parallel edge, it is 6 inches. A student multiplies 15 times 9 and gets 135 square inches, claiming that is the banner's area. Explain why this answer is wrong and calculate the correct area.
choices: The student should have subtracted the slanted side from the base first; the correct area is 36 square inches.
The student forgot to divide by 2, which is needed for all quadrilaterals; the correct area is 67.5 square inches.
The student added instead of multiplied; the correct area is 24 square inches.
The student used the slanted side instead of the perpendicular height; the correct area is 90 square inches.
hints: The lesson emphasizes that height is always perpendicular to the base, never the length of a slanted side.
When you compose a parallelogram into a rectangle using the same base and the perpendicular height, the formula is base times height, not base times slanted side.

problemText: A net is a flat pattern that can be folded into a three-dimensional solid. What does each piece in a net represent?
choices: One corner point of the solid
One vertex label of the solid
hints: Think about what happens when you unfold a box completely flat.
Each piece in the net becomes one flat surface when you fold it back up.

problemText: A rectangular prism has dimensions 5 cm long, 3 cm wide, and 2 cm tall. When its net is drawn, what are the dimensions of the top face of this prism?
hints: The top face of a rectangular prism lies opposite the bottom face and has the same dimensions.
The length and width of the prism form the length and width of the top and bottom faces.

problemText: A student draws a net for a rectangular prism and labels all six rectangles with their dimensions. When folded up, two rectangles that share an edge in the net must have one matching dimension. Why is this requirement important?
choices: So that the rectangles can fold along the edges without gaps or overlaps at the corners where the faces meet
So that the net takes up less space on the paper when you arrange all six rectangles
So that the rectangles can be drawn the same color to show which faces are adjacent
So that the two faces can fit together perfectly along that shared edge when folded
hints: Think about what happens at the fold line when you bring two faces together.
If two rectangles don't share the same edge length, they won't line up when you fold the net.

problemText: A triangular prism has two identical right triangular ends, each with legs of 6 inches and 8 inches and a hypotenuse of 10 inches. The prism is 12 inches long. To find the total surface area, a student first finds the area of both triangular faces. What is that combined area, and why must the student also find the area of three more faces?
choices: Combined triangle area is 48 square inches; the three rectangular faces wrap around each of the three sides of the triangle
Combined triangle area is 96 square inches; each triangular face must be counted twice because there are two identical ends of the prism
Combined triangle area is 48 square inches; the student needs to count six total faces to match the standard formula for all three-dimensional shapes
Combined triangle area is 120 square inches; the three rectangular faces correspond to the three dimensions of the triangle's base, height, and hypotenuse
hints: Use the triangle-area formula: base times height divided by two.
A triangular prism's sides are covered by rectangles, one for each edge of the triangular face.

problemText: A gift box shaped like a rectangular prism is 8 inches long, 5 inches wide, and 3 inches tall. A student uses a net to find the surface area and identifies three pairs of matching faces: the top and bottom, the front and back, and the two ends. If the student correctly finds that one pair has area 40 square inches and another pair has area 24 square inches, what is the total surface area?
hints: Find the area of each pair of rectangles, then add all three pairs together.
The three pairs use dimensions: length × width, length × height, and width × height.

problemText: A student is building a net for a triangular prism and makes a sketch showing two triangular faces and three rectangular faces. The student labels the triangular faces with a base of 5 cm and a height of 12 cm. The three rectangles have widths of 5 cm, 12 cm, and 13 cm, all with a height of 9 cm (the length of the prism). However, when the teacher checks the work, she points out that one edge in the net does not match. Which dimension causes this mismatch, and what does it tell us?
choices: The 5 cm and 12 cm dimensions are legs of the triangle, so they should each be the width of one rectangle, but the third rectangle width should equal the hypotenuse, which is √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13, and this does match, so there is no mismatch in the net

The 9 cm height of all rectangles represents the length of the prism and is correct for all three rectangular faces, but the rectangle widths must correspond to the three side lengths of the triangular base, and since 5² + 12² = 169 ≠ 13², the triangle cannot be a right triangle with those dimensions
The 13 cm rectangle width should be the hypotenuse of the triangle, but using 12 and 5 as legs means the hypotenuse is not 13, so the triangle and net don't match

The three rectangle widths should all equal 9 cm because the length of the prism determines every rectangular face's width in a triangular prism, and since each rectangle height is 9 cm, all widths must also be 9 cm for the net to fold into a valid prism
hints: In a triangular prism, each side length of the triangle becomes the width of one of the three rectangular faces.
Check whether a right triangle with legs 5 and 12 actually has a hypotenuse of exactly 13.

problemText: A polygon is being drawn from its vertices listed in order. After plotting all the vertices and connecting them to each other in sequence, what is the one final step you must do to complete the polygon?
choices: Check that all sides are either horizontal or vertical
Erase all the vertex points so only the sides show
Count the total number of sides to name the polygon
Connect the last vertex back to the first vertex
hints: The lesson emphasizes that a polygon must be closed with no loose ends.
Think about what makes a shape a complete polygon instead of just a connected path.

problemText: Two consecutive vertices of a polygon are at M(4, 7) and N(4, 2), where each unit is one inch. What type of side connects these vertices, and how can you tell?
choices: Vertical, because both vertices have the same first coordinate
Horizontal, because both vertices have the same first coordinate
Vertical, because both vertices have the same second coordinate
Diagonal, because the vertices do not share any coordinate
hints: Check which coordinate is the same for both M and N.
Remember: same first coordinate means the side runs straight up and down.

problemText: A parking lot outline has vertices at C(2, 5), D(8, 5), E(8, 1), and F(2, 1), listed in order. The parking lot manager needs to know the length of side CD. What is the length of side CD in units?
hints: First identify what coordinate C and D share.
Look at only the coordinate that differs, and use subtraction since both values are positive.

problemText: A decorative frame has vertices at P(-3, 2), Q(5, 2), R(5, -4), and S(-3, -4), listed in order. To draw this frame correctly, you need to identify each side and verify it is either horizontal or vertical. How many of the four sides are horizontal?
hints: A horizontal side connects vertices that share the same second coordinate.
Check each consecutive pair: P to Q, Q to R, R to S, and S back to P.

problemText: A walkway polygon has vertices at A(1, -6), B(1, 3), and C(7, 3). If you connect these vertices in order and then close the polygon by connecting C back to A, side AB runs vertically. Which statement correctly describes why you can find the length of AB using only the second coordinates?
choices: Because A and B have different first coordinates, the distance between them is determined by subtracting the first coordinates and ignoring the second coordinates
Because A and B share the same first coordinate, so the vertical distance depends only on the second coordinates
Because when the first coordinate stays constant at 1 for both points, you only need to find the distance between -6 and 3, which are the second coordinates
Because the first coordinate determines whether a side is vertical or horizontal, and once you know the side is vertical, the length comes from subtracting the second coordinates of the endpoints
hints: Look at the first coordinates of A(1, -6) and B(1, 3). Are they the same?
When a coordinate is fixed, the only measurement that changes along that line is the other coordinate.

problemText: A community plot is shaped like a trapezoid with vertices at V(-5, 3), W(-5, -2), X(4, -2), and Y(4, 3), listed in order. Each unit is one yard. To build a fence around the entire perimeter, you need to find the lengths of two adjacent sides: side VW and side WX. What is the sum of these two side lengths?
hints: Find which coordinate is shared by V and W, then which is shared by W and X.
For VW, watch whether the second coordinates are on the same side of zero or opposite sides. Do the same for WX using first coordinates.
